definitions.explanation: Coating wood or other material with many thin layers of {漆|うるし} (lacquer from the lacquer tree), and the glossy objects made this way: bowls, trays, boxes, chopsticks. Used before a noun with の: {漆塗|うるしぬ}りのお{椀|わん}.

examples.japanese: {漆塗|うるしぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{椀|わん}→お椀：06507_owan⟧。
⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{漆塗|うるしぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{箱|はこ}→箱：02162_hako⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I was given a lacquered box by my grandmother.

examples.japanese: {漆塗|うるしぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{器|うつわ}→器：11838_utsuwa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{食洗機|しょくせんき}→食洗機：19300_shokusenki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れ→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ず、⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{優|やさ}しく⟦{洗|あら}って→洗う：00827_arau⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Don't put lacquered dishes in the dishwasher; wash them gently by hand.

notes:
Japanese lacquer is so closely tied to Japan that "japan" once meant lacquerware in English. Regional styles carry place names, such as {輪島塗|わじまぬり} from Wajima. Raw lacquer can cause a rash ({漆|うるし}かぶれ).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {漆塗|うるしぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{椀|わん}→お椀：06507_owan⟧: lacquered soup bowl
- {漆塗|うるしぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{重箱|じゅうばこ}→重箱：22377_juubako⟧: lacquered tiered food box
- {漆塗|うるしぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧: lacquered chopsticks

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{漆|うるし}→漆：10584_urushi⟧: lacquer; the lacquer tree
- ⟦{漆器|しっき}→漆器：13329_shikki⟧: lacquerware (the formal word for the objects)
- 〜{塗|ぬ}り: painted, coated (as a suffix)
